dimensions.name: Relationship recovery under a prescribed specification
dimensions.justification: Track A - prescribed specification. Under the frozen true formula on the sim arm, mboostrs recovers the planted structure on held-out rows: RMSE(mu) 0.056 (SE 0.003) and RMSE(log sigma) 0.014 (0.002), better than the classical GAMLSS-style competitor at 0.123 (0.002) and 0.043 (0.005). The varying x3 slopes are recovered within sampling noise: slope(b) 1.458 (0.030) against the true 1.5, slope(c) -1.035 (0.029) against -1.0, slope(a) 0.000. Anchor 4 is not assigned: the formula handed in was the true one, so no structure was left open and its false-discovery behaviour is not exercised.

dimensions.name: Relationship discovery from data alone
dimensions.justification: Track B - data and response name only. On the sim arm mb.discover recovers the structure cleanly over 10 seeds: location precision 0.980, recall 1.000 (the x3-by-g interaction is found in 10/10), scale precision 1.000, recall 1.000 (x5), zero false discoveries among the nuisances x6/x7/x8, and zero x5-in-location or x1/x2/x3/g-in-scale traps; Gaussian is inferred in 10/10. But the same path on the real SLID arm returns an empty model (formula 1): family inference picks GammaReg for the positive log(wage) response, the boosted path does not descend, and backward elimination drops every term. Anchor 4 (screening and adoption validated on the benchmark with false-discovery behaviour characterised) is not assigned because the real-data arm collapses.

dimensions.name: Experimental iteration speed
dimensions.justification: Sim arm (3000x8): the known-spec LSS fit takes 0.279 s median (p90 0.308 s) and a drop-one-covariate what-if 0.246 s median. SLID (2007x4): 0.119 s and 0.100 s. The discovery path is about an order of magnitude slower (3.34 s sim, 1.84 s SLID per fit; 2.49 s and 1.11 s per what-if). Seconds per fit place this at anchor 3; anchor 4's sub-second refits hold for the known-spec path but the data is smaller than the standardised 50k x 20 session, which is not measured here. One catboost_uncertainty fit recorded 3404 s against a 0.76 s median - a wall-clock artifact of the shared machine - so medians are used.

dimensions.name: Uncertainty honesty (calibration)
dimensions.justification: On the heteroscedastic sim arm the known-spec 95% interval covers 0.9481 (gap -0.19 pp, SE 0.13) and the 80% interval 0.7979 (gap -0.21 pp, SE 0.27); both are within about two standard errors of nominal, and the sigma model is a function of x5, the true scale driver. On SLID the known-spec 95% interval covers 0.9548 (+0.48 pp, SE 0.19) and 80% 0.8119 (+1.19 pp, SE 0.50). Anchor 4 is not assigned: small-n and extrapolation adaptivity are not measured, and the discovery track undercovers badly on SLID (80% interval covers 0.716, gap -8.4 pp) because it returns the intercept-only model.

dimensions.name: Predictive validity
dimensions.justification: Primary loss is the Gaussian CRPS; the best competitor is a per-seed retrospective best, and comparator settings are untuned. On sim mboostrs beats the best competitor in both tracks: known-spec -4.56% (SE 0.16), discovery -4.44% (SE 0.16); RMSE -1.02% (0.14) and -0.99% (0.14). On SLID the known-spec path is at par with the best competitor (+0.58% CRPS, SE 0.13; +0.75% RMSE, SE 0.13), inside the 1% goal, but the discovery path is +34.07% CRPS (0.47) and +28.76% RMSE (0.42) because it returns the intercept-only model. Anchor 4 (competitive across the prespecified task families under matched budgets) is not assigned: the discovery track fails on the real arm.
